label: sec:phase-transitions-intro
html:
The quantum ideal gas law yields a partition function whose dominant saddle point sits inside one Hecke channel of H_n(q). Phase transitions represent the loci where this dominance shifts. We derive critical temperatures using the S^3 boundary action. This restricts the categorical action to the Hopf base S^2 of the fibration S^1 \hookrightarrow S^3_q \to S^2. The quantities [2]_q and [n_K]_q control the transition boundaries T_q^{(g \to l)} and T_q^{(l \to s)}.

We map gas, liquid, and solid states onto the symmetric, mixed, and antisymmetric Hecke channels, locating the triple point. Sublimation (the direct solid--gas transition) is recorded without a derivation: the Hecke channels are complementary summands rather than an extension of one by another, so \mathrm{Ext}^1_{H_n(q)} supplies no obstruction to the liquid phase. We present an observational test of the Z-parity sublimation rule, establishing a metallic-bonding test that separates sublimation from continuous condensation. Finally, we establish the boundary action as a canonical example of degree-0 opacity.
